title: Laptop for CAD (for TAFE Student)
body:
My son needs a laptop for his TAFE studies which includes CAD. I’m not familiar with requirements so looking for some advise fe from ozbargainers that understand the jargon.
Even budget laptops are not that cheap anymore so budget is as cheap as possible.
Requirements as follows:
💻 Laptop Recommendations for Your Studies
If you are considering purchasing a new laptop for your TAFE journey, please keep in mind that you will be using CAD and some 3D design software, particularly Vectorworks, throughout the course. A standard entry-level laptop may struggle once your drawings and design files become more complex.
For the best experience, I recommend a Windows laptop. Apple/Mac laptops are NOT recommended for this course, as even the newest struggle with the software as they are not made for CAD work (they will run it but will just freeze more often and for longer)
Recommended specifications:
• Processor: Intel Core i7 preferred, or a good modern equivalent (a recent i5/Core Ultra 5 can also perform well)
• RAM: 16 GB minimum – 32 GB is ideal if your budget allows
• Graphics: A good integrated graphics processor (GPU) at minimum, such as Intel Iris Xe / Intel Arc or AMD Radeon integrated graphics. A dedicated NVIDIA/AMD graphics card is even better, particularly if you intend to do more 3D modelling and rendering.
• Storage: 512 GB SSD minimum – 1 TB is preferable for long-term use
• Operating System: Windows 11
• Screen: Ideally 14–16", with Full HD (1920 × 1080) resolution or better
You DO NOT need to purchase an expensive gaming laptop for the course. A good-quality modern business or performance laptop with the specifications above should comfortably handle the CAD work we undertake.
When shopping, look beyond the brand name and compare the actual specifications. Sales periods such as Black Friday, EOFY, Boxing Day and back-to-school promotions can be a great opportunity to purchase a considerably better laptop for the same budget.
As a rough guide, I would prioritise your budget in this order:
Processor → RAM → Graphics → SSD storage
Try to avoid very low-powered processors, 8 GB RAM, small 256 GB drives, Chromebooks and entry-level laptops designed primarily for web browsing and basic office applications.
A suitable laptop is an investment that should ideally see you through the remainder of your TAFE studies and allow you to continue using professional landscape design software afterwards.
Keep in mind that your student laptop does not necessarily need to become your ultimate professional workstation. Once you are working in the industry and using CAD and 3D software professionally, you may choose to invest in a more powerful desktop computer and dedicated workspace setup, with larger or multiple monitors, a higher-performance graphics card and additional RAM. For now, the aim is to have a reliable, capable laptop that will comfortably support you throughout your studies without unnecessarily spending thousands of dollars.
Thanks in advance
